global_caption: The video contains 10 shots and presents a realistic-style home cooking tutorial. The setting remains stable between a clean, well-lit home kitchen and a final wooden dining area. Natural daylight combined with soft overhead lighting forms the primary lighting base. The entire video uses consistent Chinese The emotional tone remains consistently light and friendly throughout.
shot1: Shot 1 opens directly with a wide eye-level shot. Chicken cubes, green onions, ginger, garlic, cucumber, peanuts, and seasoning bowls are neatly laid out. The background features a bright, clean kitchen cabinet and stove. Warm natural light evenly illuminates the surface.
shot2: Shot 2 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, switching to a medium close-up overhead view. The cutting board dominates the frame, with ingredients arranged in sequence across foreground and background. Focus remains locked on the intersection of hands and knife blade. The kitchen background is de-emphasized to maintain instructional clarity. Warm lighting remains consistent. The chicken is cleanly diced into uniform cubes, followed by separate cuts of green onions, ginger, garlic, and cucumber. She simultaneously explains “鸡肉切丁，葱姜蒜和黄瓜分别备好”. The camera remains mostly static, with only minimal follow pan to ensure full visibility of actions.
shot3: Shot 3 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, using a close-up overhead view. A glass bowl is centered in the frame, with spoons and seasonings in the foreground and a softly blurred background preserving countertop texture. Lighting remains warm and soft, creating clean reflections on the bowl’s surface. The young woman adds salt, cooking wine, and starch to the chicken, then rapidly mixes by hand. The chicken transitions from loose to moist and evenly coated. Precise interaction between fingers and ingredients is clearly visible. The camera performs a slight push-in to emphasize textural changes.
shot4: Shot 4 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, transitioning to a medium close-up overhead view. A small seasoning bowl is centered in composition. Sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, and a small amount of starch are added sequentially, forming clear procedural layers. Background remains the same countertop environment, with unchanged lighting. Liquids are stirred with chopsticks, quickly blending from layered to uniformly translucent. The camera performs a slight overhead circular movement to help viewers observe the mixture state.
shot5: Shot 5 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, shifting to a medium close-up slightly angled downward. The stove and pot opening occupy the right side of the frame, with a strainer and empty plate on the left for depth. Side lighting highlights the pot edge and peanut surface. The young woman pours peanuts into hot oil on low heat, gently frying them. Peanuts move slightly in oil, turning more golden. They are quickly scooped out with a strainer and removed. She explains “花生小火炸香，先盛出来保持脆感”. The camera performs a short lateral pan along the pot edge, then gently pushes in to emphasize heat control.
shot6: Shot 6 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, using a medium eye-level slightly side-angle view. The pot surface becomes the absolute focal point. The edge of the spatula appears in the foreground, while the background stove remains simple. Under warm light, the oil surface reflects soft, bright highlights. After heating the pan and adding oil, dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns are added. The spices jump rapidly in oil, releasing aroma and instantly activating their color. She clearly announces in Chinese “锅里留底油，下干辣椒和花椒，小火爆香”. The camera performs a slight tilt-follow from the pot edge, enhancing the layered impact of spices hitting the oil.
shot7: Shot 7 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, switching to a medium close-up slightly upward angle with a noticeable push-in. After chicken is added to the pot, it occupies the center of the frame. Steam and spatula form dynamic foreground obstructions. Background kitchen lights blur into soft warm spots. The chicken rapidly changes from translucent to opaque and shiny, edges slightly curling. Sleeve and steam follow movements realistically. The camera continuously pushes forward, reinforcing the sense of speed and transformation during stir-frying.
shot8: Shot 8 connects with the previous shot via a hard cut, employing a composite motion from overhead to eye-level. Composition guides diced cucumber, peanuts, and sauce entering the pot from the top of the frame. Ingredients inside the pot form distinct color layers. Warm main lighting remains consistent, creating wet reflections on the sauce surface. The young woman quickly adds diced cucumber, returned peanuts, and prepared sauce. The spatula continuously flips ingredients, efficiently mixing them over high heat. Cucumber retains crispness, peanuts stay firm, and sauce begins to adhere. The camera first slightly lowers, then follows the stir-fry direction with a lateral pan, emphasizing critical heat control in the tutorial.
shot9: Shot 9 connects with the previous shot via match-cut editing, transitioning to a close-up eye-level view. A partial section of the pot fills the frame. Shallow depth of field keeps focus firmly on chicken and sauce surface. Background is fully blurred into warm color blocks. Sauce transitions from flowing to thickened, bubbles become finer, and glossy sheen evenly coats chicken, cucumber, and peanuts. Material changes are clearly discernible. She slows her pace, stating “看到汤汁收亮、均匀挂住食材就可以了”. The camera performs a macro-style slow push-in, clearly conveying the crucial pre-completion state.
shot10: Shot 10 gently dissolves from the previous shot, using a medium-long shot at eye level that slowly pulls back. The finished dish is transferred from the wok to a white plate on a wooden table. In the foreground, the freshly plated Kung Pao chicken is displayed, while the background reveals the still-bright and warm kitchen environment. Finely chopped green onions are evenly sprinkled over the top as the final touch. A young woman stands in front of the wooden table, looking directly at the camera, and concludes with a natural and friendly tone “这样做出来鸡丁嫩、花生脆、口感酸甜微辣，关键就是花生先盛出，最后大火快速收汁”. The soft The camera slowly pulls back, fully revealing the finished dish, the person, and the surrounding environment, bringing the tutorial to a clear and satisfying conclusion.
